comments.body:
### Third occurrence — this one presented as **needs-auth**, not wrong-principal

Hit again on `spark-facilitator/20260820-0817` (ACE Phase 3), 2026-08-24/25. Same root cause, but a **different surface** than the two prior occurrences, which is worth recording because it changes what the operator sees.

**What was different:** the session's nova MCP exposed **only** `authenticate` / `complete_authentication`. `get_hq_connection`, `list_apps` and `list_projects` were all unresolvable via `ToolSearch` — so there was no principal to compare, and the usual "list_apps shows the wrong project" discriminator was structurally unavailable. Occurrence 2 by contrast bound a live-but-wrong principal (stale June apps in project `f0369b78-4b29-4c76-b1a6-e7c74fe0040b`).

**The PAT was verifiably fine, in the same session.** Direct `curl` to `https://mcp.commcare.app/mcp` bearing the key from `~/.ace/env.sh`:

- `get_hq_connection` → `{"configured":true,"server":"production", ...}` with `connect-ace-prod` in `available_domains` — so the PAT **does** carry `nova.hq.read`.
- `list_apps` → returns the run's real apps, `64ec7be2-…` (Learn) and `6f997f65-…` (Deliver), in project `5686b544-dd71-41fa-8d3f-632534473020`.

So the credential on disk is correct and complete; only the connection binding is wrong. Same conclusion as before, reached without the `list_apps` discriminator.

**One interaction worth flagging for anything that auto-clears the needs-auth cache.** `~/.claude/mcp-needs-auth-cache.json` held a stale `nova` entry at session start. ACE's preflight auto-cleared it — but that clear necessarily lands *after* the session has already bound its MCP connections, so it does nothing for the session that observes the failure. The cache reads clean while nova stays dead in-session, which makes the state look healthier than it is on any subsequent inspection. Whatever clears that cache can't help the current process; it only helps the next one.

**Restart is still not sufficient on its own** — consistent with occurrence 2, where the halting process had itself started well after the prior halt and bound the same wrong credential. `/mcp` → nova → **Clear authentication** (not `Authenticate`, which mints a fresh OAuth token and re-binds while reporting success) → then quit and reopen.

Happy to grab any additional in-session state next time it fires if there's something specific that would help isolate it.

comments.author: jjackson
comments.body:
### Correcting my comment above — it is **not** stored-credential precedence, at least not here

I attributed this to a stored OAuth credential outranking the PAT. The client logs disprove that, so I want to correct it rather than leave a wrong mechanism sitting in the thread.

`~/Library/Caches/claude-cli-nodejs/<worktree>/mcp-logs-plugin-nova-nova/*.jsonl`, at connection time:

```
Executing headersHelper to get dynamic headers
Successfully retrieved 0 headers from headersHelper
HTTP transport options: {"headers":{"User-Agent":"claude-code/2.1.243 (cli)","Accept-Encoding":"identity"},...}
No access token in storage
Generated new OAuth state
HTTP Connection failed after 513ms: Unauthorized
```

Two things fall out of that:

1. **`No access token in storage`** — there was no stored OAuth credential. `Clear authentication` had been working the whole time; it simply was never the relevant lever. That's why clearing it repeatedly changed nothing.
2. **`Successfully retrieved 0 headers from headersHelper`** — the helper took its `else printf '{}'` branch, so no `Authorization` header was ever attached. The endpoint 401s and advertises `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer resource_metadata=…`, so the client does the correct thing and starts OAuth. The OAuth cascade is a *symptom*, not the cause.

**Scope of it here:** the helper returned 1 header in 1235 logged sessions and 0 in 79. Last good `2026-08-21T16:11:46Z`, first bad `2026-08-21T18:00:16Z`, and every one of the 54 sessions since has been 0.

**What it isn't:** not the plugin — the 1.24.0 (last working) and 1.26.0 (first broken) trees are byte-identical apart from the version string, and the helper text is unchanged through 1.28.0. Not the Claude Code build that installed that day — 2.1.239 landed 2h20m *after* the break. Not the key or the env files — `NOVA_API_KEY` is present in the `claude` process env, `~/.zshenv` and `~/.ace/env.sh` both predate the break unchanged, and running the helper by hand emits a correct header.

**The fragile seam,** whatever tripped it: the helper resolves `$NOVA_API_KEY` from the environment it is spawned into, and on this machine that variable arrives via `~/.zshenv` — which is **zsh-only**. Anything that executes the helper through `/bin/sh`, or with a sanitized environment, cannot see it. Confirmed: `env -i /bin/sh -c` does not see the variable; `env -i zsh -lc` does.

**Worth considering regardless of the trigger:** the `else printf '{}'` branch converts "I could not find the key" into "this server has no auth," which is indistinguishable downstream from "this server uses OAuth." That is what sent three separate debugging sessions at the credential and at `Clear authentication`, neither of which was ever involved. Failing loudly, or emitting a header the server can reject with a distinguishable error, would have made this ~5 minutes instead of ~4 days.

**Workaround, for anyone hitting it:** skip the helper entirely —

```
claude mcp add --transport http --scope user nova https://mcp.commcare.app/mcp \
  --header "Authorization: Bearer $NOVA_API_KEY"
```

Connects immediately and resolves to the right project. Tools land as `mcp__nova__*`, which the bundled `nova-architect-autonomous` agent already declares alongside the plugin-prefixed names, so the skills keep working. Trade-off is the key sitting in plaintext in `~/.claude.json`.

Also, since it may be a separate issue: the authorize URL is built with no scopes (`Scopes in URL: NOT FOUND`, `No scopes available from URL or metadata`), and a token obtained that way comes back without `nova.hq.read` — `get_hq_connection` then reports `scope_missing`. So OAuth is not a viable fallback for anything touching HQ, which is what made this fully blocking rather than merely annoying.

comments.author: jjackson
comments.body:
### Final correction — I had this wrong twice. Here is the actual cause, with a same-session control.

Apologies for the churn. My first comment blamed stored-OAuth precedence; my second blamed a zsh-vs-sh env seam and implied Claude Code's version was ruled out. Both were wrong. I kept digging and the picture is now clean.

**The trigger is a Claude Code change at 2.1.238.** Correlating every logged nova connection on this machine against the client version in the same log:

| version | sessions | sent a header |
|---|---|---|
| … ≤ 2.1.237 | 32 (at .237) | **32** |
| **2.1.238** | 3 | **0** |
| 2.1.239 / .241 / .243 | 50 | **0** |

Last good session `2026-08-21T16:11:46Z` on 2.1.237; first bad `2026-08-21T18:00:16Z` on 2.1.238. **0 of 53 sessions on 2.1.238+ have ever sent a header.** There is precedent: 2.1.202 broke it the same way (6/6) and 2.1.205 fixed it.

**But it is not a blanket Claude Code regression — and this is the part that matters for the plugin.** The `canopy` plugin also ships a `headersHelper` on an http server. In the *same sessions*, on the *same version*, both plugin-scoped:

```
2026-08-25T02-44-19-241Z v2.1.243  plugin-canopy-canopy-web  hdr=1   ← works
2026-08-25T02-44-19-241Z v2.1.243  plugin-nova-nova          hdr=0   ← does not
2026-08-25T02-54-22-397Z v2.1.243  plugin-canopy-canopy-web  hdr=1
2026-08-25T02-54-22-397Z v2.1.243  plugin-nova-nova          hdr=0
```

The difference is what the two helpers depend on:

- **canopy** reads a token **file** (`~/.claude/canopy/workbench-token`). Its own comment says *"there is no env var to export."* Unaffected.
- **nova** reads the **environment variable** `$NOVA_API_KEY`, and on the else branch emits `{}`. Affected.

So 2.1.238 appears to have changed what environment `headersHelper` receives at interactive-session connect time, and only env-dependent helpers notice.

**Things I ruled out, so nobody repeats the work:** not the plugin (1.24.0 and 1.26.0 trees are byte-identical but for the version string; helper text unchanged through 1.28.0). Not header filtering — I probed a synthetic http server and `{"Authorization":…}` passes through intact (`retrieved 1 headers`), alone or alongside another header, in either case. Not the helper string — nova's verbatim helper returns `retrieved 1 headers` when attached to a project-scoped server. Not the shell or the user's env files, which are unchanged and predate the break.

**Note for anyone trying to reproduce from the CLI: you can't.** The `claude mcp list` health-check path still passes the full environment — I confirmed the helper runs under `/bin/sh` with 50 vars including `NOVA_API_KEY` present. Only the interactive session path drops it. That divergence is why this looked unreproducible for days.

**Suggested fix, and it is small:** make the helper not depend on the ambient environment — the way canopy's already does. Reading the key from a file (or falling back to one when the env var is unset) would have made the plugin immune to this entirely. Failing loudly instead of `printf '{}'` would help just as much: emitting an empty object turns "I couldn't find the key" into "this server has no auth," which is indistinguishable downstream from "this server uses OAuth," and that is what sent three separate debugging sessions at the credential and at `Clear authentication` — neither of which was ever involved.

I'll also file this against `anthropics/claude-code`, since the 2.1.238 behaviour change is theirs; happy to link it here once it's up.

Workaround for anyone blocked meanwhile, unchanged:

```
claude mcp add --transport http --scope user nova https://mcp.commcare.app/mcp \
  --header "Authorization: Bearer $NOVA_API_KEY"
```
